newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - June 25.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents.
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- BUDGET 'WILL AIM TO DAMPEN SPENDING'

The Ernst & Young Item Club, the independent forecasting group, has predicted that chancellor Gordon Brown will deliver a deflationary summer Budget next month in order to damp down domestic demand and rescue industry from the effects of higher interest rates and a strong pound. The group, which uses the Treasury model to make its forecasts, is expecting taxes to be raised by around 5 billion stg to prevent consumer spending becoming too strong.
-- SCOTTISH POWER IN RACE FOR GROWTH

Scottish Power, the multi-utility, has signalled its intention to take 15 per cent of the electricity supply market by 2000. The group has also targeted a 12 per cent share of the competitive gas market. The details of the group's ambitions come amid concern by some analysts about the profitability of Scot Power's planned electricity expansion, and doubts about its ability to dent the dominant position of British Gas. -- CBI ATTACKED OVER 'TILT' FOR A SINGLE CURRENCY

Employers' organisation the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) has been criticised for attempting to 'bounce' members into supporting European economic and monetary union. The group, which has been staging a regional roadshow on the issue of Emu, has denied that the presentations have been too heavily biased towards British entry of a single European currency.
THE TIMES
-- CPS TAKES ON CRIMINAL CASE AGAINST REGAN

The private criminal proceedings begun by the Co-Operative Wholesale Society against Andrew Regan, who failed in his takeover bid of the company, have been taken over by the Crown Prosecution Service. The CPS will also take over prosecutions against David Lyons, Regan's adviser, as well as Allen Green, former Co-Op manager, and has asked the police to make further investigations. The Times newspaper reports that Norton Rose law firm, asked by Hambros Bank to conduct an independent inquiry into the Co-Op bid, has failed to interview Regan, Lyons, Green and CWS directors.
-- OIL FIRMS SLIP INTO 110M STG LOSSES

The Petroleum Industry Association has revealed that oil companies in the UK lost a total of 110m stg in 1996 on gross sales of 41bn stg, compared to a pre-tax profit of 94m stg in 1995. The losses have been blamed on tight retail margins brought on by competition within the supermarkets and overcapacity among refiners. Industry analysts expect that the trend will continue in 1997, leading to further consolidation within the sector.
-- GEC'S DEFENCE LOOKS ARM LOOKS FOR MERGER PARTNERS

Sir Geoffrey Pattie, the chairman of GEC Marconi, has announced that GEC's defensive arm is seeking merger and alliance partners, in particular those from foreign countries. Pattie lauded the benefits of cross-border mergers at a defence industry conference in Brussels on Tuesday, declaring GEC will vote for an alliance 'if the shareholders are better served' by it, adding that an merger between British Aerospace and GEC has been ruled out.
THE GUARDIAN
-- HALIFAX: WE'LL PLAY IT SAFE

The head of the Halifax, Britain's second largest bank, has warned that reckless lending by building societies and banks over the last year could result in 'horrible problems' for the financial services sector. Chief executive Mike Blackburn made the comments in an interview with The Guardian in which he also sought to reassure investors by pledging that the Halifax should spend its surplus cash on extra dividends and share buy-backs.
-- JOBS CRISIS WILL HIT EURO, SAYS GEORGE

Eddie George, the governor of the Bank of England, has issued a warning on the dangers of introducing a single European currency amid high unemployment in many EU countries. Speaking on Tuesday night, George admitted to being 'frankly nervous' at the prospect of bringing in the euro when there were very high and very different rates of unemployment across Europe.
-- SHAREHOLDERS PUT BOOT INTO SEARS

Directors of retail group Sears have been criticised by shareholders over the dismal performance of the shoes and Selfridges chain. The shareholders blasted the award of a 465,000 pounds stg pay-off to ousted chief executive Liam Strong, and attacked the quality of the directors and the company's track record. Sears released a mixed trading statement Tuesday, reporting that like-for-like sales for the first 19 weeks of the year up 2.5 per cent on the same period last year, but they had been ahead by 5.3 per cent in the first 11 weeks.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- SMITHKLINE HALTS TRIALS IN ARTHRITIS DRUG SETBACK

SmithKline Beecham, the pharmaceuticals and healthcare company, has said that late-stage trials of a significant new drug to treat rheumatoid arthritis have had to be stopped due to a potentially dangerous effect on the immune system of patients. The drug was one of 10 'blockbusters' that SmithKline had intended to release before the year 2000, and had potential peak sales of about 300 million stg.
-- FILL YOUR TROLLEY WITH A TV WHEN YOU SHOP AT TESCO

Supermarket group Tesco is planning to roll out the sale of televisions in almost 300 of its stores around the country over the next two months. The move, which has been described as 'high risk' for Tesco by one retail analyst, is also expected to effect profits at high street electrical retailers such as Dixons and Comet. The Asda and Sainsbury's supermarket chains are already involved in the brown goods market, and Safeway is also known to be talking to suppliers about introducing electrical goods.
-- TELEWEST DENIES CWC TAKEOVER TALKS

Cable company Telewest Communications has 'emphatically denied' reports that it is involved in takeover talks with Cable & Wireless Communications (CWC), the new telecoms and cable company formed by the merger of Cable & Wireless's Mercury subsidiary with three other cable firms. However, a spokesman for Telewest also refused to rule out the possibility of a merger at some stage in the future.
